name: China
hook: Confucius, the Yangtze and Mao: four thousand years of clues distilled into six things.

facts.label: Confucius
facts.statement: Confucius, born in 551 B.C. and also called Kongfuzi or "Master Kong," briefly served as prime minister of the state of Lu.

facts.label: Mandarin
facts.statement: Mandarin, called Putonghua or "the common language," is China's standard language; Pinyin romanization was officially adopted in 1979.

facts.label: the Yangtze
facts.statement: The Yangtze, China's longest river, runs from Tibet to the East China Sea, and the Chinese alligator survives in its valley.

facts.label: Tibet
facts.statement: Tibet is a high-altitude autonomous region China incorporated in 1951 amid controversy.

facts.label: Hong Kong
facts.statement: Hong Kong was ceded to Britain in 1842 and became a crown colony; I.M. Pei's Bank of China Tower now marks its skyline.

facts.label: Taiwan
facts.statement: Taiwan, which Portuguese sailors named Ilha Formosa or "beautiful island," is served by EVA Air and China Airlines.

facts.label: Mao and Chiang Kai-shek
facts.statement: Mao Tse-tung's victory at Huai-hai in 1948 drove Chiang Kai-shek from the mainland in December 1949.
